en: Tears poured from his eyes.
His mind reeled in anguish;
Such was that grievous day.
Then mighty Seytek’s
Eyes blazed like fire.
The enraged boy
Was seized by bloodthirsty fury.
His broad front teeth were like a gate,
His other teeth fearsome,
Sharp as a sword
And broad as a wrist;
He ground them again and again.
The extraordinary young wretch
Was seized by bloodthirsty fury.
“Jeti-Özön is no land of mine,
The Jediger are no people of mine.
I have been wandering as an exile,
Parted from my fierce lion of a father,
My formidable warrior father!
I have been looking upon Kyyaz
As though he stood in my father’s place.
Though still alive, my precious soul
Has been living as one dead!
Against Kanchoro, who felled the banner,
And Kyyaz, who burned it,
Let me rise and wreak slaughter;
For my father gone to the other world,
Let me take vengeance now!
My elder Külchoro has been disgraced,
His stallion hidden so he could not mount it.
Why did you not tell me, Mother,
Your doomed kinsman was dying?
My falcon, my dearest kin,
My precious uncle, my inheritance!
Where is Talas, where is that land,
And where are the Kyrgyz people of Talas?
Why should the offspring of a lordly lion
Wander as a fugitive?
Where is my heroic uncle now,
And where is the road back to our people?
Where is the mighty foe I can unhorse,
Where is the land that will shelter me?
Where is the enemy I can engage?
My dear uncle, my gray-maned lion,
My true blood has begun to boil!
Our livestock grazes in alien valleys,
And our lives have dwindled to a handful.
Where are the Ala-Too valleys
Where one may gallop freely,
And the people whose villages stood together?
What use is wavering?
Does the cautious man not also die?
Must this wretched head not suffer
Whatever God has ordained?
Will the dug grave not hold
All beneath the sun?
The black earth swallows everyone
When the true decree arrives
And the angel reaches out five fingers.
When the taker of souls
Draws near to take your life,
Does not mortal man die
Even at the sight of his broad encampment?
Must not every living mortal submit
To the fate inscribed by the Creator?
Can the offspring of a noble house prosper
By wandering homeless?
If I do not make the prince’s heir
Cease to live as an outcast;
If I do not make it seem
As though one man set the whole world aflame;
If I have strength, I will battle,
If I have power, I will strike,
And unless my destined hour has come, I will not die.
If driven to desperation, Jediger,
May I divide all your countless riches,
Measuring each share with my whip.
If I do not bind and capture
Your champions alive,
And cast turmoil
Among all your lionhearted heroes;
If I do not test your courage,
And, should the Jediger of Jeti-Özön
Fall wholly into my hands,
Divide your goods by measure of my whip;
If I do not make the slaughter glorious
And drive your lithe young women
Back to the Kyrgyz;
If I do not test your khan’s courage,
And carry off the brutal Jediger
As plunder;
If I do not bring misery upon their bey,
And thus avenge
My father, the lordly lion!
My hapless mother, so this is your homeland;
The Jediger took you as spoil,
And you brought me here
After your life was laid waste.
Why should the offspring of a prince
Wander as a fugitive?
My hapless mother, where are our people?
Will a day come when we return to them?
Why should a prince’s own son
Live on the run?
My ill-fated mother, where are our people?
Why did you hide it and not tell me sooner?
Why did you conceal my forefather,
The formidable Manas, Mother?
On distant journeys, our road will be one;
When battle begins, our arms will be one.
My noble uncle Külchoro,
Falcon against the many-shaped foe;
My noble father’s hero,
Foremost among my champions—
If I do not bind my falcon, my lionhearted uncle,
Close beside me at my waist;
Then make Keng-Kol our frontier
And set all before us ablaze;
Smash their ranks and bring them suffering,
And, if true fate comes, fall to a bullet;
If I do not grapple with them and wreak slaughter;
If I do not rescue and reunite
Old Bakai, left to me by my forefather,
And my poor mother Kanykei;
If I do not restore my noble sister-in-law Akbala
And give her back to my uncle!
If I do not gather without fail
The scattered Nogai and countless Kyrgyz;
Bring back all that was lost,
And make good all that is lacking;
Place my golden crown
Upon my long-imprisoned uncle;
Subdue the whole world
And proclaim it to the people;
If I do not raise my uncle as khan
Over every last one of those dogs!
If I do not make him a fortress upon the black earth,
A lord who governs the people,
A blessed and sacred man,
A khan before all who behold him;
If I do not make my heroic uncle Külchoro
My sovereign!
If I do not breach the enemy’s bounds
And wreak immeasurable slaughter;
If I do not grapple with treacherous Kanchoro
And gouge out his eyes;
If I do not hunt down
And torment all who became our enemies,
How could I remain a fugitive?
A man is born and slaughters sheep,
Heroes feast and slaughter for celebrations,
The people cry aloud and give him a name;
A prince’s only son
Cannot pass his days a captive.
The offspring of a noble prince
Cannot wander in flight like this.
When I stiffen in wrath,
I shall destroy the hostile foe.
My precious uncle Külchoro,
The inheritance left by my heroic father—
If I do not bind him close beside me;
If I do not earn the name “son of the formidable one,”
And feed the hostile enemy’s countless herds
To the people in Talas;
If I do not raid caravans and seize their trains,
Contending until I take revenge;
Strike their paradise and seize their migrations,
Fighting until I take revenge;
I have stiffened in wrath—
May I perish if I do not wage bloody war this year.
If the enemy provokes my rage,
May I perish if I do not take his head by the sword.
If I do not plant the banner with a shout
And turn my warhorse’s head toward battle;
If an enemy appears before me
And I do not destroy them all at once;
If I do not take up a sword bare of sheath
And spread slaughter through the age;
If I do not crush my enemies
And take their heads this year,
May I die unworthy of the name Seytek,
May I sink away as though never born.
Confidant of my formidable father,
Companion of the prince,
Their sheep shared the same fold,
Their food shared among comrades,
Their gains gathered together—
He was Semetey’s own contemporary.
